nodes.line: You are not from around the corner, are you.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. I am sending back 79 papers a day from Cabramatta and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. That's it. That's the whole ask.

Do not laugh. They will drop my Cabramatta order if I can show $45 of turnover on the other side of the shop by the long weekend. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Better Rate, Cabramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. I do the Cabramatta round from the back of seven and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. If anyone asks, you were never here.

Two people have already said no. There is a dog on the Cabramatta round that has had two of my bags and a docket book that was not even mine. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Dog on Ash Street, Cabramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Nine of us at Cabramatta have gone in on the same numbers since the long weekend and one of us has stopped putting money in. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I'll see you right for it.

You are the first person to stop all morning. The agency at Canley Vale closed six months before Cabramatta started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Other Agency, Cabramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. There has been a car in the Parramatta yard since school holidays with a whiteboard with last March still on it on the passenger seat and no owner answering. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. That's it. That's the whole ask.

Do not laugh. Now that it is documented, Parramatta is owed $50 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Unclaimed Falcon, Parramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. I am in my first year at Parramatta and I have to log 66 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. If anyone asks, you were never here.

Two people have already said no. Somebody has been coming into the Parramatta yard after half six to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Air Line, Parramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Ashwin, the bloke whose car it is at Parramatta

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. My car has been at Parramatta since school holidays and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $66. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I'll see you right for it.

You are the first person to stop all morning. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Parramatta works out of Tramway Avenue, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: My Own Car, Parramatta — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Ah. Someone with two working legs.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. People leave things at the Auburn roller door after the back of seven and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. That's it. That's the whole ask.

Do not laugh. The photos worked, which means Auburn can claim back the $59 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since a public holiday nobody remembered. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: Dumped Out the Back, Auburn — that's done.
The Tip Fee, Auburn — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Something came into Auburn on a public holiday nobody remembered in a box of paperbacks that I do not think the family meant to give away. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. If anyone asks, you were never here.

Two people have already said no. Two people have been coming into the Auburn sorting room since a public holiday nobody remembered and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Good Box, Auburn — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. I do the Auburn pick-ups in a van with 47 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I'll see you right for it.

You are the first person to stop all morning. Everything Auburn cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Lidcombe, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.
Before you start: did anyone see you.
No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
